title: Intra- and interspecific competition interact: multi-factorial experiments in two tit species
content:
Abstract
Many species exhibit negative density-dependent reproduction as competition for limited resources increases with breeding density. We studied two closely-related species that partly compete for access to the same resources (blue tits [BTs] Cyanistes caeruleus and great tits [GTs] Parus major). We aimed to test for interactive effects among breeding densities of either species to study how the magnitude of negative intraspecific density-dependent clutch size regulation changes with fluctuations in the competitor species' density. We manipulated the availability of “blue tit” and “great tit” boxes in a full factorial design to experimentally change the species' breeding densities. We found that breeding cavities were limiting: BT breeding pairs increased when BT box densities were increased from “low” to “high”; GT breeding pairs, similarly, increased when GT box densities were increased from “low” to “high.” Increased GT box densities further increased the number of BT breeders in GT boxes, but only when BT box densities were low, implying that GTs outcompeted BTs for access to “great tit” boxes. BT clutch sizes were negatively affected by BT box densities, but only when GT box numbers were high, too. Those patterns were also echoed in other key reproductive traits and were significantly species-specific, implying that the strength of intraspecific and interspecific competition interacted to affect reproductive performance.
